claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of the official Child Benefit guidance, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

There are two key reasons why you cannot claim Child Benefit:

1. **Another person has priority**: You've indicated that another claimant who lives with Alex has priority for the claim. Under Child Benefit rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. If someone else who lives with Alex has priority, they would be the one entitled to claim, not you.

2. **Alex has been in local authority care too long without sufficient home time**: Alex has been in local authority care for 9 weeks, which exceeds the 8-week limit. Normally, Child Benefit stops after 8 weeks in care. However, there is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home. Since Alex does not spend 24 or more hours per week at home, you do not qualify for this exception.

Either of these factors alone would prevent you from claiming Child Benefit, and unfortunately both apply in your situation. If you believe your circumstances have changed or you have questions about the priority claimant situation, you should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly.

1. **Another claimant who lives with the child has priority**: According to the guidance, 'Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.' If another person who lives with Alex has priority for the claim, they would be the eligible claimant, not you. The guidance states that 'If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit.'

2. **Child in local authority care for 9 weeks without spending 24+ hours/week at home**: The guidance clearly states that after 8 weeks in care, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit. There is an exception 'if they spend at least 24 hours a week at home,' but in Alex's case, they do not spend 24+ hours per week at home. Since Alex has been in local authority care for 9 weeks (which exceeds the 8-week limit) and does not meet the exception criteria, this makes you ineligible for Child Benefit.

Either one of these factors alone would be sufficient to make you ineligible, but both apply in this situation.
